correctness.rationale: All parameter ranges and definitions are explicit. Cauchy–Schwarz gives the mixed-shore bound using sums of incidences, and an exact factorization (t−1)(q²−t)≥0 covers t=1 through q². The optimal-palette lower bound uses packing-size capacities and excludes k=v; exhaustion of (v,1) and (v−1,2) low-colour sizes and frozen singleton names yields the star graph. Both independent finite programs were executed successfully: full named Fano enumeration and reduced PG(2,3) enumeration; these are crosschecks, not substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The published projective-plane palette size and maximum independent-set lemma are antecedents. The new independently proved statements classify all optimum named colourings, count their singleton-name assignments, establish a mixed-shore near-maximum gap, and identify every optimal one-vertex recolouring component as a q²-leaf star. Actual published-finding corpus searches by aliases, parameters, and implications retrieved related but non-dominating findings. The 2019 primary text was inspected at the relevant theorem and searched for recolouring. Priority is not absolute.

value.rationale: An all-order classification of minimum named packing colourings on a canonical family of incidence graphs, including non-Desarguesian planes, resolves the natural optimum-state mobility problem left undecided by the known χρ value. The rigid division into 2v(v−1)! q²-leaf stars and the large fragmentation are meaningful geometric structure, not a routine recitation of the previously published palette threshold.
